claims.text: Pregnancy test is required, regardless of sexual or menstrual history.
claims.quote: A pregnancy test is required , even before menarche, if it is possible that ovulation has started. Pregnancy should not be excluded based on sexual or menstrual history.

claims.text: Primary amenorrhea with normal secondary sex characteristics: start with pelvic ultrasound for outflow obstruction.
claims.quote: If patients have primary amenorrhea and normal secondary sexual characteristics, testing should begin with pelvic ultrasound to check for congenital genital tract obstruction.

claims.text: Common blood tests: FSH (ovarian insufficiency), TSH, prolactin, and total testosterone or DHEA-S.
claims.quote: Additional blood tests that are commonly done (to exclude specific etiologies) include: Follicle-stimulating hormone (ovarian insufficiency); if the level is high, it should be remeasured monthly at least twice Thyroid stimulating hormone (thyroid disease) Prolactin (if the level is high [hyperprolactinemia], it should be remeasured) Total serum testosterone or dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (PMOS or other causes of hirsutism or virilization)

claims.text: High FSH points to ovarian dysfunction; low FSH and LH with normal TSH points to hypothalamic or pituitary dysfunction.
claims.quote: Amenorrhea with high follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism) suggests ovarian dysfunction. Amenorrhea with low FSH and LH and normal TSH levels (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism) suggests hypothalamic or pituitary dysfunction.

claims.text: Headaches, visual field defects or pituitary dysfunction: brain MRI.
claims.quote: Patients with headaches and visual field defects or evidence of pituitary dysfunction require brain MRI.

claims.text: Progestin challenge (secondary amenorrhea with normal prolactin, FSH and thyroid tests, no virilization): withdrawal bleeding means estrogen is sufficient.
claims.quote: If patients have secondary amenorrhea with normal prolactin and FSH levels and normal thyroid function and do not have virilization, a trial of a progestin can be given to try to evaluate estrogen status. If the estrogen level is sufficient, a course of a progestin should stimulate withdrawal bleeding after the progestin is stopped
